summary: User USB port (USB-OTG, full speed) as a USB CDC device with TinyUSB: the PC sees a COM port (VID 0xCAFE, PID 0x4000).
readme: TinyUSB CDC example: the minimal TinyUSB project; Windows shows a serial port, msh `cdc_example` echoes what the PC sends (USB_CH_SEL low = USB-FS)
fsp_note: TinyUSB drives the USB controller itself (rusb2); the FSP only has to route the USBFS interrupts to usbfs_*_handler in ra_gen/vector_data.c (the openmv FSP does; board/tinyusb/drv_tinyusb.c defines them and replaces the weak stubs).

ports.what: drv_tinyusb.c (USB interrupts, FS/HS select), usb_descriptors.c, cdc_example.c

patches.what: every rt_pin_mode() called R_IOPORT_Open(), which re-applies the whole FSP pin setup: after the app's board layer set its LED/KEY pins, USB_CH_SEL went back high (USB-HS path) and the PC never saw the CDC device

source_checks.what: USBFS interrupts in the FSP vector table (FSP_PROJECT openmv has them)

notes: Two USB-C ports: ART-Link (debug + console) and the user USB-OTG port - the CDC port needs a second cable on the user port.
VID 0xCAFE / PID 0x4000 are TinyUSB's test IDs - fine on the bench, not for a product.
Found on the board 2026-10-31: without the drv_gpio.c patch the PC sees no USB device (USB_CH_SEL high again after the board layer's rt_pin_mode calls).
PKG_TINYUSB_DEVICE_PORT_SPEED: the SDK project's rtconfig.h has 0x00 (older package index); this PC's index gives 0x0200 (explicit full speed) for the same choice.
evidence: SDK VISION-BOARD 1.3.0 projects/usb/vision_board_tinyusb_hid, _msc, _uvc (same TinyUSB port and SConstruct line)
